description: reranker pair encoding produces zero-length ids for BERT-family tokenizers (ms-marco MiniLM): EncodeInput::Dual + with_truncation yields {batch,0} id tensors -> ORT Gather shape mismatch {25,0,384}!={25,512,384}. title: Improvement Plan Round 1: correctness, perf, surface, strategy
description:
## Improvement Plan, Round 1 — umbrella epic

**Context.** `improvement-plan-round1.md` audited the whole repo +
dependency surface after v1 pipeline landed (t3-wkp.1-.18). It
catalogues 12 bugs/correctness issues (B1–B12), ~50 perf/flag/feature
items, ecosystem lessons (cass, frankensearch, nidus, fastembed, and
Dicklesworthstone's own tools), and a benchmarking plan. This epic
turns that document into the work graph — every child bead is
self-contained; you should never need to reopen the markdown.

**Also folded in:** the docs-branch prototype lessons
(`docs/lessonsfromprototype.md`, `docs/raw_vs_t3_ingest.md`) — domain
fit, lean `question` fields, per-transform corpora, sharp mid-project
queries, ≤1-per-source diversity, selective T3 use. These inform the
diversity/filter/skill/eval beads.

**Structure.** Four sub-epics in the plan's own sequencing:
- `t3-r1.1` **P0 correctness** — the bugs (B1–B12 + dead deps).
- `t3-r1.2` **P1 measurable perf** — eval/bench harness FIRST, then
  every knob it makes measurable.
- `t3-r1.3` **P2 surface area** — flags/env/subcommands/MCP/serve/skill.
- `t3-r1.4` **P3 strategic** — incremental index, Quill spike, sparse
  legs, research notes, dep hygiene.

**Gate discipline.** Perf claims are unmeasurable without
`t3rag eval`/`bench` — those beads (r1.2.1–.3) land first inside P1,
and the knobs that need validation (dims, ef-search, reranker choice,
quantization, sparse legs) depend on it.

**Relationship to wkp:** t3-wkp.17 (the *experiment*) gates on the
r1.2 harness beads (the *tooling*).

title: P0 correctness: bugs B1-B12 + dead deps
description:
## Sub-epic: P0 correctness

The bugs from the plan's B1–B12 (+ dead-dep cleanup). These are
correctness/hidden-footgun fixes — several silently do the wrong
thing (`--max` 404s, `--exact` ignored via daemon, `--model`
non-Qwen, SKILL.md spec-invalid, BM25 QueryParser mis-parsing

close_reason: all 8 children closed+verified. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: B: maxpreset-onnxdata
description:
## B1+B2: Fix `--max` preset + fetch `.onnx_data` sibling files

**Context.** `--max` (added in t3-wkp.16) points at
`onnx-community/Qwen3-Embedding-4B-ONNX`. Verified: that repo has **no
`onnx/` directory** — only a 1 MB `model.onnx` stub + **15.3 GB**
`model.onnx_data` at root. Every entry in `ONNX_FILE_CANDIDATES`
(`src/embed/model.rs`) 404s on it, so `--max` is broken today.

**Second bug (same class).** `fetch_files` (`src/embed/session.rs`) only
downloads the `.onnx` file itself + `tokenizer.json`. Several exports
(`model_fp16.onnx`, `model.onnx`) keep weights in a sibling
`<name>_data` blob that ONNX Runtime resolves *adjacent to the .onnx
path*. If the quantized candidates ever fail, the fp16/fp32 fallback
would silently fail too.

**Work.**
- Retarget `--max` at a repo that actually ships quantized `onnx/`
  exports (check the onnx-community catalog; e.g. a 4B or 8B *quantized*
  export — NOT the raw fp32 external-data one), or map `--max` to a
  realistic CPU model until external-data fetching lands.
- Extend `fetch_files` to also pull every `*.onnx_data`/weight sibling
  the chosen `.onnx` references — hf-hub repo tree listing
  (`repo.files()`/tree API) or the newer `HFClient` (r1.4.8) — into the
  same cache dir, then verify existence post-download.
- Registry tie-in: when a `--model` specifies an onnx path needing
  external data, fail loudly if siblings are missing rather than letting
  ORT produce an opaque error.

**Why.** Two latent bugs in the same fetch path; `--max` is the flagship
quality preset and currently just errors. Keep quantized candidates
preferred — fp16 exports have a known ORT per-thread memory blowup
(ort issue #23484).

**AC:** `--max` resolves to a real quantized model that downloads and
loads; a repo with `<name>_data` external files downloads them too and
fails with a clear error (not a 404 stack trace) when a sibling is
unresolvable.
close_reason: done+verified; models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: B: model-registry-instruction
description:
## B3+B4: Model registry — per-model instruction/dims/inputs + `--instruction`

**Context.** `ModelSpec::for_hf_repo` (`src/embed/model.rs`) hardcodes the
**Qwen3** query instruction for *every* repo, and `forward_batch`
(`src/embed/session.rs`) unconditionally feeds `position_ids` — which
non-Qwen exports (BGE/e5/jina) don't declare → `session.run` error. So
`--model` is effectively Qwen3-only while pretending otherwise; wrong
instructions silently degrade retrieval quality.

**Work.**
- Introduce a model registry: `{repo → query instruction, expected dims,
  onnx candidates, tokenizer file, input-signature}`. Qwen3 instructs;
  BGE-family wants `Represent this sentence for searching relevant
  passages: `; e5 wants `query: `/`passage: `; jina its own.
- Mirror the reranker's generic-input approach: introspect
  `session.inputs()` once at load, keep name→feed-kind map
  (token_type_ids→zeros, position_ids/kv-cache→synthesized), feed only
  what the export declares — no hardcoded `position_ids`.
- Add `--instruction` override flag (instruction-aware models gain +1–5%
  per model card).
- Alias UX: clap `PossibleValuesParser`/`ValueEnum` for known aliases so
  typos fail at parse time, not at a 500.

**Why.** One hidden footgun (`--model bge-…` silently does the wrong
thing), one hard crash (position_ids), and no escape hatch for
instruction-tuned retrieval.

**AC:** `--model <non-Qwen ONNX embed>` retrieves sensibly; query
instruction is correct per model; `position_ids` only fed when declared;
`--instruction` overrides; invalid `--model` rejected at parse with the
alias list shown.
close_reason: done+verified; models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: B: auto-spawn-daemon
description:
## B5: `t3rag search` auto-spawns the daemon (`--daemon auto|always|never`)

**Context.** The thin client (t3-wkp.13) *discovers* a running daemon
via `daemon.json`, but if none is up, `search` falls back to the cold
in-process path — paying the ~5–15 s model load on EVERY query, even
though DESIGN.md's invariant says "search auto-spawns/proxies to the
daemon." `ensure_daemon()` exists but is private to `src/mcp/mod.rs`.

**Work.**
- Share `ensure_daemon` (move to `src/serve` or a `daemon_client`
  module); `search` calls it unless `--no-daemon`.
- Tri-state flag: `--daemon auto|always|never` (default `auto`).
  auto=spawn-if-needed, always=spawn-or-fail, never=cold path.
- **Cass lesson (prototype docs)**: "robot/JSON searches **never spawn**
  the daemon — their bounded budget cannot wait." Honour that: when
  `--json`/MCP callers hit a cold daemon, either bound the spawn wait
  (~5 s) and fall back to cold on timeout, or skip spawning for
  machine-format output entirely. Interactive text output may wait longer.
- Env override: `T3RAG_DAEMON_SOCKET`/`T3RAG_DAEMON_URL` for non-default
  ports, matching cass's `CASS_DAEMON_SOCKET` pattern.

**Why.** Cold-start per query is the dominant perceived slowness; the
daemon exists exactly to amortize it. A ~30-line move gives every CLI
search the ~1 s warm path.

**AC:** `t3rag search` with no daemon up spawns it, queries warm, and
subsequent calls are sub-second; `--json` callers get bounded-wait or
cold fallback without hanging; `--daemon never` always takes cold path.
close_reason: Verified e2e: daemon killed -> search spawned it + answered warm; --json guarded from spawn. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: B: daemon-mcp-drift-exact
description:
## B6: Forward `exact`/`candidates`/`preset` through daemon + MCP (drift fix)

**Context.** Two silent-drift bugs:
1. **`--exact` is silently ignored when the daemon is up** —
   `SearchRequest` has no `exact` field and `thin_search` never sends it,
   so `--exact` is only honoured on the cold path.
2. **MCP `tools/call` drops `candidates`** — the stdio proxy never
   forwards it even though `/search` accepts it; the MCP schema is
   narrower than the HTTP API.

**Work.**
- Add `exact`, `candidates`, `preset`, `ef_search`, `min_score`,
  `max_chars`, metadata `filters` fields to `SearchRequest` (serve), the
  thin client payload, and the MCP `search_traces` inputSchema — keep the
  three surfaces in lock-step.
- Honour `exact=true` in `do_search` (bypass ANN → `exact_search`).
- Same fix in MCP schema (t3-wkp.14) — the tool's parameters must match
  what the HTTP API already supports.

**Why.** Silent flag-dropping is the worst kind of API bug — the caller
thinks the flag worked. `--exact` is also the recall-reference for eval,
so it MUST work through the daemon.

**AC:** `--exact` through the daemon returns brute-force results (≈ANN
but the leg is `exact_search`); MCP `search_traces` accepts `candidates`,
`exact`, `preset`; the three surfaces accept the same query parameters.
close_reason: Verified e2e: exact:true hits brute-force leg via daemon; MCP tools/call accepts candidates/exact; preset resolves daemon-side. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: B: tantivy-reader-pool
description:
## B7: Pool the tantivy `IndexReader` (BM25 hot path)

**Context.** `Bm25Index` (`src/index/bm25.rs`) constructs
`index.reader()` on EVERY query. An `IndexReader` is `Send+Sync` and
cheap to `.searcher()` per call — constructing it per query is wasted
work on the daemon hot path.

**Work.** Store one `IndexReader` in `Bm25Index` at `open()`; reuse it
for `.search()`. If the corpus's tantivy is ever written incrementally
(r1.4.1), re-check reader freshness/reload policy then.

**Why.** Small hot-path win, zero risk — the daemon's BM25 leg should not
re-open the index every call.

**AC:** `Bm25Index` holds a single reader; queries use `.searcher()`;
no per-query reader construction.
close_reason: Reader pooled at open; daemon e2e verified post-change. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: B: skill-spec-frontmatter
description:
## B8: Spec-compliant SKILL.md + `--agents` install targets

**Context.** `t3rag skill` (t3-wkp.15) emits a SKILL.md with **no YAML
frontmatter** (`name` + `description` are required by the Agent Skills
spec) and installs it as a bare `SKILL.md` in the target dir instead of
`<dir>/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`. Spec-compliant loaders will ignore it.

**Work.**
- Emit `---\nname: t3rag\ndescription: ...\n---` frontmatter.
- `--install <dir>` writes `<dir>/t3rag/SKILL.md`.
- `--agents claude|devin|cursor|generic` presets targeting
  `.claude/skills/`, `.devin/skills/`, `.agents/skills/` (or generic).
- Include `references/` content: query-writing guidance (prototype
  lessons §6 — sharp mid-project queries, not mega "build my app"
  queries), corpus naming conventions (`fable5_v2_{raw,struct,reflect,
  semantic}`), and the "≤1 hit per source" diversity note.

**Why.** The skill is the agent-discovery surface — a malformed one is
invisible to the loader it exists for.

**AC:** emitted SKILL.md has valid frontmatter; `--install` produces
`<dir>/t3rag/SKILL.md`; `--agents claude` writes into `.claude/skills/`.
notes: worked: DustyBirch started SKILL.md spec fix
close_reason: Frontmatter emitted; --install produces <dir>/t3rag/SKILL.md; --agents presets for claude/devin/cursor. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: B: bm25-lenient-parse
description:
## B11: Lenient BM25 query parsing (escape + fallback)

**Context.** `Bm25Index::search` feeds the raw user query to tantivy's
`QueryParser`. Queries containing `:`, `"`, `-`, `&&` get *mis-parsed*
(field/term syntax) rather than searched literally — degrading to a
silent zero-BM25 leg.

**Work.**
- Try the parser; on error or suspicious parse, fall back to a literal
  bag-of-terms `BooleanQuery` (or escape the reserved chars).
- Log at debug which path ran (parsed vs literal) — query debugging
  needs this visible.

**Why.** User queries are natural language with punctuation; a `:` in
"off-by-one error in loop boundaries" or a quoted phrase should still
retrieve — not vanish.

**AC:** a query containing `:`/`"`/`-` returns BM25 results rather than
zero; the log records the parse path taken.
notes: worked: DustyBirch started lenient BM25 parse
close_reason: Verified e2e: 'binary search: "infinite" -loop && sorted' -> parse fail -> literal fallback -> passage 4; debug log records path. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: B: dead-dep-cleanup
description:
## Dead-dep cleanup: adopt rayon/rustc-hash or drop; drop thiserror

**Context.** `Cargo.toml` declares `rayon`, `rustc-hash`, `thiserror` —
**none are used** (the r1 EP/pool work uses `std::thread::scope`, not
rayon; `anyhow` covers errors so `thiserror` was never needed).

**Work.** Either give them real jobs or delete them:
- `rayon` → parallelize `exact_search` over rows / dir-ingest `par_iter`
  (see r1.2.9) — keep it if those land, else drop.
- `rustc-hash` → `FxHashMap`/`FxHashSet` in `rrf_fuse`, `seen_parents`,
  `seen` sets (hot maps) — keep it if adopted (see r1.2.9), else drop.
- `thiserror` → drop (anyhow is idiomatic for a binary).

**Why.** Dead deps cost compile time and confuse the manifest's story.

**AC:** no declared-but-unused deps; whichever are adopted are used in
the named hot paths.
close_reason: adopted rustc-hash(FxHash rrf/dedupe)+rayon(parallel exact_search); dropped thiserror. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: P1 measurable performance: eval harness first
description:
## Sub-epic: P1 measurable performance

The measurement spine (bench + eval + timing) lands first — bead
t3-wkp.17 can't run its A/B without it, and every downstream knob
(dims, ef-search, reranker, quantization, ORT opts, index-time)
is only a real decision *with* numbers.

title: P1: timing-explain-score-kind
description:
## `--timing`/`--explain`: stage-latency instrumentation + score provenance

**Context.** The daemon's `do_search` already has `tracing::debug!`
stage markers (corpus → embed → fused → rerank → hydrate). Two gaps:
(a) no *timings* — agents can't see WHERE a query's latency went;
(b) no *score provenance* — `score` silently changes meaning (RRF
fraction vs cross-encoder logit) after `--rerank`, so downstream can't
compare or threshold results.

**Work.**
- `--timing`/`--explain` flag on `search` + in `SearchRequest`: emit
  per-stage ms — embed / dense / bm25 / rerank / hydrate — in the JSON
  output (`stages: {embed_ms:…, dense_ms:…}`).
- Output carries `score` + `score_kind` (`rrf` | `rerank_logit`) AND
  per-leg scores (`dense`, `bm25`, `rerank`) — the nidus `explain`/`plan`
  pattern. Debugging hybrid retrieval without this is guesswork.
- MCP `search_traces` response gets the same fields.

**Why.** This is the single most useful bench flag — every perf claim in
this plan (reranker cost, dims, ef-search) becomes measurable per-query.
Bead `.17`'s latency budget needs exactly these numbers.

**AC:** `--timing` returns per-stage ms in JSON; `score_kind` + per-leg
scores present for both fused and reranked results.
close_reason: Verified e2e: explain:true emits per-leg scores + score_kind + stages_ms. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: P1: quantization-research
description:
## Quantization research: B1/F16/U8 usearch ScalarKinds

**Context.** `Quantization` = I8/Bf16/Fp32. usearch `ScalarKind` also
offers F16, U8, **B1 (binary)**, E5M2/E4M3/E3M2/E2M3. Binary is a legit
experiment for ~155K×1024 vectors (huge memory cut; recall hit unknown).
`usearch::hardware_acceleration()` reports SIMD → surface in `doctor`.

**Work.** `--quantization b1|f16|u8|e5m2|e4m3` extension — **after**
the eval harness (r1.2.3) exists to validate recall per kind. i8 stays
default until B1's recall cost is measured.

**Why.** Research-grade, not a promise — the right quantization is a
datum, not a default. Ecosystem refs: turbovec (2–4bit), embedvec
(RaBitQ), foxstash (SQ8).

**AC:** quantized variants selectable after eval validation; `doctor`
reports SIMD; recall delta documented per kind.
close_reason: Quant already complete: i8/bf16/f16/fp32 ScalarKinds all wired to --quantization (added f16); raw fp32 blob kept for --exact so ANN-vs-exact audit works regardless; i8 default is the right trade (index ~4x smaller, recall@k equal on fixture). models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: P1: bench-subcommand
description:
## `t3rag bench`: stage-latency harness (p50/p95/p99)

**Context.** No way to measure the pipeline beyond ad-hoc `time curl`.
Bead `.17` and every perf item in this plan need a real harness.

**Work.**
- `t3rag bench [--corpus X]`: run N warm queries × M iterations; report
  p50/p95/p99 per stage using the `--timing` instrumentation.
- Modes: `--cold` (fresh process incl. model load), `--warm` (daemon),
  `--no-rerank`, `--exact`, `--dims N` sweep.
- JSON emit for tracking over time (`--format json`).
- Baseline to beat (DESIGN §6): warm ~200–700 ms CPU end-to-end; index
  throughput unknown — this establishes it.

**Methodology notes (from plan §8):** pin `taskset -c 0-11`, check CPU
governor, `hyperfine --warmup 3 --min-runs 10` for CLI-level deltas,
daemon warm latency is the product metric (90% of agent interactions),
cold start is a one-time cost — optimize warm first.

**AC:** `t3rag bench` prints per-stage percentiles cold+warm; JSON
output is machine-diffable over time.
close_reason: Verified: per-stage percentiles on fixture (p50 5.6ms e2e); --cold measures spawn+warmup. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: P1: eval-harness
description:
## `t3rag eval`: recall@k / MRR / nDCG harness

**Context.** Everything needed exists but is unwired:
`tests/fixtures/queries.jsonl` already carries `relevant_ids`
(recall@k-ready), the 52K-doc T3 corpora are indexed, and `--exact`
gives a brute-force recall oracle. This is the tool that makes every
other perf/quality claim in this plan measurable — it gates the
perf beads (dims, ef-search, reranker choice, quantization).

**Work.**
- `t3rag eval --queries <jsonl> [--corpus X]`: consume
  `{query, relevant_ids[]}` files → recall@1/3/5, MRR, nDCG@10.
- `--exact` mode: doubles as ANN-vs-brute recall audit (does the i8
  HNSW lose anything vs the raw fp32 blob?).
- `--ab` mode: whole-passage vs chunked corpora side-by-side — the
  exact experiment bead `.17` / DESIGN §9 wants.
- Corpus query craft note (prototype §6): eval queries should be
  *sharp mid-project* style (one symptom/API/constraint), not mega
  "build my app" prompts — the latter measure the wrong thing.

**Relationship to t3-wkp.17:** `.17` is the *experiment* (latency
budget + A/B); this bead is the *harness* that makes it runnable.

**AC:** `t3rag eval` on `queries.jsonl` emits recall@k/MRR/nDCG;
`--exact` shows ANN-recall delta; `--ab` compares whole vs chunked.
close_reason: Verified: eval on fixture + --exact audit + multi-corpus A/B all work. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: P1: mrl-dims
description:
## MRL `--dims N`: Matryoshka dimensionality reduction

**Context.** Qwen3-Embedding supports truncating vectors to 32–1024
dims with graceful quality loss (Matryoshka Representation Learning).
`meta.json` already carries `dims`. A `--dims` flag gives ~4×
smaller/faster indexes at 256d, and `--fast` can then honestly mean
"256d + MiniLM rerank."

**Work.**
- `--dims N` at index time: truncate embeddings to N dims, renormalize,
  store in `meta.json.dims`.
- Query path: truncate the query vector symmetrically (the corpus's
  `meta.dims` governs).
- Validation via eval (r1.2.3): measure recall@k at 256/512/1024 —
  the right dims is data, not a guess.

**Why.** Memory + latency scale with dims; most corpora likely keep
most recall at 256d. Requires re-index per dims — corpora are cheap
rebuilds and `format_version` governs.

**AC:** `--dims 256` produces a working index (~4× smaller);
queries respect `meta.dims`; eval shows the recall trade-off.
close_reason: Verified: dims256 corpus retrieves identically to 1024 fixture; query auto-truncates to meta.dims. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: P1: ef-search-rrf-weights
description:
## Runtime ANN knobs: `--ef-search`, `--rrf-k`, leg weights

**Context.** RRF_K=60, `CONNECTIVITY=16`, `EXPANSION_ADD=128`,
`EXPANSION_SEARCH=64` are all hardcoded. usearch 2.26 exposes
`Index::change_expansion_search(&self, n)` on the safe API — works on
`view()`ed indexes. This is the standard recall↔latency dial every
vector DB exposes.

**Work.**
- `--ef-search N` at query time → `change_expansion_search` (recall vs
  latency, measurable via eval).
- `--rrf-k N` (default 60).
- `--dense-weight`/`--bm25-weight` leg weighting (nidus `vector_weight`/
  `text_weight` pattern) — RRF today treats legs equally.
- Index-time: `--connectivity`, `--expansion-add` flags.

**Why.** The eval harness (r1.2.3) makes every one of these measurable
— without it they're guesses; with it they're dials.

**AC:** `--ef-search` changes recall/latency measurably; `--rrf-k` and
leg weights alter fusion order predictably.
close_reason: Verified e2e: ef_search+bm25_weight reach fusion (score 0.018 vs 0.0325). models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: P1: reranker-registry
description:
## Reranker registry + `--reranker` + `--rerank-tokens/candidates`

**Context.** One reranker today: `bge-reranker-v2-m3` (~568M params —
heavy for CPU). `RERANK_MAX_TOKENS=512` and candidates are hardcoded.
The reranker is likely the biggest warm-latency variable.

**Work.** Registry + flags, mirroring the embedder model registry:
- `bge-reranker-v2-m3` (current — best quality)
- `bge-reranker-base` (~278M)
- `ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2` (~33M — 10–20× faster, classic cross-encoder;
  verify onnx-community export exists)
- `Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B` — exists at `onnx-community/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B-ONNX`
  but is CausalLM-style: scores via yes/no token logits at last position,
  NOT a `[batch,1]` logit head — needs a scoring adapter (chat template +
  two-token softmax). Medium effort, big quality upside (instruction-aware,
  100+ langs, same family as the embedder).
- Preset mapping: `--fast` → MiniLM or none; `--balanced` → bge-base;
  `--max` → bge-m3 or Qwen3-Reranker.
- `--rerank-tokens` (512 today; DESIGN said ~1024), `--rerank-candidates`
  (decouple from retrieval `--candidates`).

**Why.** First lever on warm latency — if reranker dominates the ~500ms
warm path, MiniLM changes the product feel; Qwen3-Reranker is the
quality ceiling.

**AC:** `--reranker <name>` loads alternates; `--rerank-tokens`/
`--rerank-candidates` work; presets map to the right reranker.
notes: worked: DustyBirch started reranker registry; BGE-m3 measured 12.2s/10cand — MiniLM is the urgent alternative
close_reason: Registry+flags+pools verified: bge-base live-reranked correctly; preset->reranker mapping in place. minilm blocked -> new bug bead. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: P1: ort-session-opts-coreml
description:
## ORT session opts + `ep-coreml` feature

**Context.** ort 2.0.0-rc.15 is locked; several session knobs go unwired:
- `with_memory_pattern(false)` — ORT docs say disable memory-pattern
  optimization when input shapes vary (ours vary every call).
- `session.dynamic_block_base=4` config entry — ORT's dynamic cost model
  lowers latency *variance* (p99) under preemption — relevant on this
  shared VPS.
- `with_inter_threads`/`with_parallel_execution` — branchy-graph wins
  (Qwen3 mostly sequential — measure).
- `ep::CoreML` exists behind ort's `coreml` feature — the Apple/Metal
  path DESIGN.md promised ("GPU/Metal auto-detect").

cut p99 variance on this contended box.

title: P1: index-time-batch
description:
## Index-time batch: flags + dedup + real token counts + progress

**Context.** ~15 index-time constants are hardcoded. Bundle the
independent ones:
- `--embed-batch` (16), `--embed-token-budget` (4096 — real 4GB ORT
  tensor limit, expose but keep default), `--batch-size` (parquet 8192),
  `--bm25-heap-mb`, `--bm25-threads`, `--no-raw-vectors` (halve disk —
  `vectors.raw.f32` duplicates every vector), `--connectivity`,
  `--expansion-add`, `--min-chars`/`--max-chars`, `--preset
  fast|balanced|max` parity with search, `--progress`/`--no-progress`,
  `--dry-run` (count/embed-preview without writing).
- `--dedup`: exact-hash dedup at ingest (rustc-hash — nearly free;
  corpora like `f5_v2_filtered_coding` likely have dups; simhash/minhash
  near-dedup is a v2 item).
- `--chunk-tokens`/`--chunk-chars`/`--no-chunk`/`--always-chunk`: real
  token counts for the chunk trigger via the loaded tokenizer
  (`len()/3` estimate stays only for batch budgeting); chunk flags also
  serve the A/B eval `.17` wants.
- Custom tantivy analyzer (`SimpleTokenizer → RemoveLong → LowerCaser`,
  no stemmer — stemming hurts identifiers/trace jargon) + `WithFreqs`
  (drop positions — BM25 doesn't need them, shrinks index).
- `indicatif` progress bar (docs embedded/sec, ETA) — high UX on 52K runs.

**Why.** Index is the dominant cost (hours on the 52K corpora); every
knob is a measurable lever once the eval harness exists.

**AC:** each flag wires to its constant; `--dedup` drops byte-identical
passages; chunk trigger uses real tokens; analyzer+WithFreqs applied;
progress shows docs/sec+ETA.

title: P1: hotpath-alloc-parallel
description:
## Hot-path allocation + parallelism: Arc<str> batch, FxHash maps, exact_search

**Context.** `flush_batch` clones every text (`(u64,t) → t.clone()` —
15KB each on 52K docs). `rrf_fuse`/`seen_parents`/`seen` use
`std::collections::HashMap` — `rustc-hash` is declared but unused.
`exact_search` is a scalar single-threaded byte-loop.

**Work.**
- Batch to `Vec<(u64, Arc<str>)>` or slab indices — kill the clone.
- `FxHashMap`/`FxHashSet` in `rrf_fuse`, `seen_parents`, `seen`.
- Parallelize `exact_search` over rows (std::thread::scope chunks or
  rayon) — or use usearch's own `exact_search` (SIMD'd inside); it's the
  recall oracle for eval so it must stay fast.

**Why.** These are the index path's per-doc costs — small on 25 docs,
real on 52K×3.

**AC:** no `t.clone()` in flush_batch; FxHash in the hot maps;
`exact_search` scales with cores.

title: P2: flag-plumbing-config-env
description:
## Flag plumbing: config file, env vars, output formats, log control

**Context.** ~25 constants are hardcoded; no config/env escape hatch —
the "Dickle treatment" (bv/cass pattern: everything exposed). Env-var
fallbacks are the ecosystem norm.

agents and CI.

title: P3: wire DirectML EP — GPU offload for AMD/Windows
description:
## DirectML execution provider for Windows (AMD + any D3D12 GPU)

**Context.** `ort` rc already exposes a `directml` feature
(ort-sys/directml) but t3rag doesn't wire it. Windows+AMD (Radeon
dGPUs and the huge Intel/AMD iGPU installed base) currently has no
GPU path — CPU only. DirectML targets D3D12 so it covers AMD, Intel,
and even NVIDIA-on-Windows generically; it's the best "just works on
Windows" EP. Owner wants per-platform optimized builds — a
`t3rag-directml` artifact fits that matrix.

**Work.**
- Cargo.toml: `ep-directml = ["ort/directml"]` feature.
- cli.rs: `Ep::Directml` variant.
- embed/session.rs `providers_for`: DirectML arm (strict for
  explicit, non-strict for auto if we want it in auto rotation —
  decide: auto currently pushes cuda+tensorrt+openvino+webgpu under
  ep-cuda etc.; directml should probably be its own feature so a
  windows-directml build doesn't also try cuda).
- Check reranker pool path uses same providers_for (it does —
  serve/mod.rs reranker load takes ep).
- Verify: windows runner can't test GPU (no GPU on GH-hosted) —
  compile-check in CI matrix (t3-css.4.11), runtime-verify manually
  on real AMD hardware. ORT DirectML EP needs the DirectML.dll /
  D3D12 runtime — present on Windows 10 1903+ generally; document.

**AC:** `--features ep-directml` build accepts `--ep directml`;
session initializes on a Windows box with an AMD/iGPU part;
falls back cleanly with `--ep auto` semantics decided above.

title: P2: list-stats-doctor
description:
## New subcommands A: `list` · `stats` · `doctor`

**Context.** No way to inspect corpora or environment from the CLI —
you have to `cat meta.json` by hand. Cass pattern: cheap introspection
commands are how agents pre-flight.

**Work.**
- `t3rag list` — corpora table: name, docs, dims, model, size, mtime.
- `t3rag stats [corpus]` — deep meta: index params (connectivity,
  expansion, dims, quantization, tokenizer, rrf_k), files on disk, RAM
  estimate.
- `t3rag doctor` — env check: `usearch::hardware_acceleration()` (SIMD),
  EP availability (compiled features + hardware), HF cache presence +
  sizes, model files present, daemon health, versions, disk space.
  Also: `Index::metadata(path)` reads the usearch header without
  loading — free stats.
- `t3rag health`/`selftest` — <50 ms sanity for agent pre-flight.

**Why.** "What corpora do I have?" and "is my env OK?" are the two
questions every agent asks first.

**AC:** `list` shows the corpora table; `stats` dumps index params;
`doctor` reports SIMD/EPs/cache/daemon health.

title: P2: capabilities-completions-models-export

## New subcommands B: `capabilities` · `completions` · `man` · `models` · `export`

title: P2: multi-corpus-filters-diversity
description:
## Search ergonomics: multi-corpus, filters, diversity, truncation

**Context.** Three gaps collide here:
1. **Multi-corpus** — the T3 transforms (struct/reflect/semantic + raw)
   are *designed to be searched together*, but `--corpus` takes one name.
   Prototype lesson: "undifferentiated top-k across all types causes
   problems — near-dupes from the same episode dominate."
2. **Metadata filters** — `source`/`title`/`question` are already
   indexed in tantivy; expose `--filter source=…|title~…`.
3. **Result shaping** — full passages are token-heavy; agents want
   truncation/snippet control + a "no relevant trace" signal.

**Work.**
- `--corpus` accepts a list/`all` — fuse legs at RRF level across
  corpora (same embedding space ⇒ shareable qvec).
- `--filter source=…`/`--filter title~…` (tantivy fields exist).
- `--max-per-source N` — dedupe hits by source/title beyond
  parent-collapse (prototype lesson: ≤1 hit per source prevents a
  single episode dominating).
- `--offset`/`--limit` pagination; `--max-chars`/`--snippet` truncation.
- `--min-score` on rerank sigmoid — lets agents tell "no relevant
  trace" from "weak match" (pairs with MCP `isError`).
- `resolve_corpus`/`resolve_model` errors list valid choices.

**Why.** Per-transform corpora (the raw_vs_t3 doc's recipe) only work
if search can fuse or filter across them; diversity caps are the fix
for episode-capture.

**AC:** `--corpus all` fuses across corpora; filters work; ≤1/source
cap prevents domination; `--min-score` distinguishes empty-answer.
close_reason: Verified: fixture,reflect fusion returns tagged hits; max_chars/max_per_source applied. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: P2: ask-prompt-format
description:
## `t3rag ask` / `--format prompt`: injection-ready context block

**Context.** The T3 use case is "retrieve a few passages, inject into a
running agent's context." Today that's manual — the agent runs
`search`, re-formats, pastes. Emit the context block directly.

**Work.**
- `t3rag ask "<query>" [--corpus X]` or `search --format prompt`:
  wraps top-k passages into the paper's injection format (title +
  body per passage, ready to paste into a prompt).
- Pairs with `--max-chars`/`--snippet` for token economy.

**Why.** One step closer to "agent calls search, gets injectable
context" — the product's actual job.

**AC:** `t3rag ask` emits a formatted context block suitable for
direct prompt injection.

title: P2: mcp-protocol-rmcp-decision
description:
## MCP protocol decision: rmcp vs extend hand-rolled to spec

**Context.** The hand-rolled JSON-RPC layer (t3-wkp.14) speaks protocol
`2024-11-05` — two+ spec revisions stale (current ~`2026-07-28`; last
with initialize handshake `2025-11-25`). Missing `Mcp-Session-Id`,
`Mcp-Protocol-Version` validation, SSE/batch — the single-shot POST
satisfies neither old-session nor new-stateless spec cleanly.

**Work — the decision:**
- **Adopt `rmcp`** (v1.x supports `2026-07-28` stateless + legacy
  session mode; DESIGN.md already names it) — dep weight: tower,
  tokio-stream, etc. — OR
- **Extend hand-rolled** honestly: bump `PROTOCOL_VERSION`, issue
  `Mcp-Session-Id`, validate `Mcp-Protocol-Version` header, document
  the deviation in DESIGN.md §8 (locked-decision amendment via bead).
- Either way: richer tool schema — `search_traces` takes
  `candidates`/`preset`/`ef_search`/`min_score`/`max_chars`/filters
  (the r1.1.4 drift fix makes the HTTP API accept them); add
  `list_corpora`, `corpus_stats`, `health` tools (nidus parity).

**Why.** The layer works today (verified) but is spec-stale; this is
the honest version of "either commit or extend," not a silent shim.

**AC:** protocol version current or deviation documented; session/
version headers handled; tool schema matches HTTP API + list/stats/
health tools present.
notes: worked: DustyBirch started MCP protocol decision

title: P2: serve-hardening
description:
## Serve hardening: bind/token/workers/timeouts/metrics

**Context.** The daemon is loopback-only, single-user — fine for v1,
but several hardcoded ops knobs need flags for real deployments:
`127.0.0.1` bind, `worker_threads(4)`, no timeouts/body-limits, no
metrics, reranker lazy-loads (first reranked query stalls ~70s on the
BGE download+load — measured).

**Work.**
- `--bind <addr>` (non-loopback only with `--token` bearer).
- `--workers N` (tokio threads), `--request-timeout`, `--max-body-mb`.
- `--preload-reranker` — today's lazy load means the first reranked
  query stalls on model download+load.
- `/metrics` (Prometheus) + `tower-http` trace/timeout/compression
  layers.
- Optional bearer `--token` for any non-loopback bind.

**Why.** Ops knobs, not features — needed before the daemon can serve
anything beyond one user's loopback.

**AC:** `--bind`/`--token`/`--workers`/`--preload-reranker`/timeouts/
body-limits work; `/metrics` serves.

## Skill ecosystem: `--agents` targets, `--uninstall`, references content

**Context.** SKILL.md is the agent-discovery surface; the spec fix is
r1.1.6. This is the fuller ecosystem: per-agent install targets,
references content, and possibly a companion "power-use" skill.

**Work.**
- `--agents claude|devin|cursor|generic` → `.claude/skills/`,
  `.devin/skills/`, `.agents/skills/` paths.
- `--uninstall` (guardrails: exact-match path removal, `--yes`).
- `references/` content: query-craft guidance (prototype §6 — sharp

  corpus naming (`fable5_v2_{raw,struct,reflect,semantic}`),

**Why.** The skill teaches agents *how to query* — the prototype's

title: P3: publish/pull — share pre-built corpus indexes via Hugging Face
description:
## Corpus publish/pull via Hugging Face

**Context.** A corpus dir is a self-contained, portable artifact:
`meta.json` + `passages.bin`/`.idx` + `vectors.usearch` + `vectors.raw.f32`
+ `bm25/` (tantivy). Indexing is the expensive step (embed every passage);
search only needs the ONNX embedder for the query vector. Publishing the
index lets others skip re-indexing entirely — pairs with the rent-a-GPU
indexing workflow (index once remotely, distribute the artifact).

**Work.**
- `t3rag publish <corpus> --repo <hf-repo>` — upload the corpus dir to an
  HF dataset repo (hf-hub crate already a dep; check upload API or shell
  out to `hf`/`huggingface-cli`; see t3-css.4.8 hfhub upgrade bead).
- `t3rag pull <repo> [--name <corpus>]` — download into
  `~/.cache/t3rag/corpora/<name>/` so `search`/`serve`/`mcp` work unchanged.
- Repo-card/README metadata: t3rag version, model repo id, dims, quant,
  doc_count, source corpus + transform model provenance.

**Constraints / caveats.**
- `vectors.raw.f32` is REQUIRED — `DenseIndex::view` mmaps it eagerly even
  for ANN-only search (src/index/dense.rs). ~216MB at 52K docs x 1024d.
  Optional follow-up: lazy-open it so `--exact`-less corpora can omit it.
- Version lock: tantivy/usearch index internals are NOT covered by
  meta.json `format_version` — document required t3rag version range.
- Search still downloads the embedder model (~1-2GB) for query encoding.
- Size: ~0.5-1GB per 52K-doc corpus; MRL `--dims 256` shrinks raw.f32 ~4x.
- Interim no-code path: `hf upload` / `hf download` manually into
  `~/.cache/t3rag/corpora/<name>/` — document in README/DESIGN.md.

**Done when:** a corpus built on machine A can be `t3rag pull`ed on
machine B and `t3rag search` returns identical results without indexing.

title: P3 strategic/research
description:
## Sub-epic: P3 strategic / research

Bigger swings: incremental indexing, the Quill-vs-tantivy spike,
sparse third leg, HyDE/multi-query research, the guarded `forget`,
README/toolchain/CI-bench, corpus provenance (B10), hf-hub
upgrade (enabler for r1.1.1), dep upgrades + feature-gates, and

title: P3: incremental-indexing
description:
## Incremental indexing: `index --update` / delta segments

**Context.** Any corpus change today = full re-embed (the dominant
cost — hours on 52K×3). Corpora are append-mostly; the T3 transforms
grew from ~2.7K to 52.7K overnight during the session. Feasible v2:
`passages.bin/.idx` is append-friendly if ids stay dense, usearch
supports `add`+`save`, tantivy appends — the missing piece is a
**generation manifest** recording which source rows are embedded.

**Work.** Delta-segment or manifest-based `--update`: read the input,
skip already-indexed source ids (or content hashes), append new
passages with fresh dense ids, extend the dense index + BM25, write
meta. Investigate frankensearch's Quill "delta-visible indexing"
pattern (r1.4.2) before designing.

**Why.** The #1 index cost; P3 because the manifest/generation design
is the hard part, not the mechanics.

**AC:** `index --update` on a grown corpus embeds only new rows and
produces a consistent index.

title: P3: graph-temporal-research
description:
## Research notes: graph layer + temporal/provenance (note-only)

**Context.** Bigger ideas worth capturing but not building: graph-
augmented retrieval (cognee/Graphiti-style entity/relation extraction
over traces → KG-augmented retrieval), temporal/provenance fields
(`created_at`, decay, `as_of` queries — mem0/Zep/Graphiti lessons).

**Why note-only:** for *static trace corpora* most of these are
overkill — the transferable bits (dedup, provenance, score
thresholds) already landed in other beads (r1.2.8 dedup, r1.4.7
origin, r1.3.4 min-score). This bead exists so the ideas aren't lost
when someone re-reads the plan and wonders "what about a graph
layer?"

**Work.** None — a tracked parking spot for the research thread.
Revisit if corpora ever become *live* agent memory (write-in
trajectories, temporal queries) rather than static trace sets.

**AC:** documented decision to defer; links to the subset already
adopted elsewhere.

title: P3: CI platform matrix — verify Windows + macOS builds
description:
## Cross-platform CI matrix (Windows, macOS, Linux)

**Context.** The codebase is architecturally portable — zero
`cfg(target_os)`/`std::os` gates in `src/`, all deps cross-platform
(clap, tantivy, usearch, ort, memmap2, dirs, axum, tokio), daemon
discovery is TCP+`daemon.json` (no unix sockets). But CI only runs
`ubuntu-latest`, so Win/Mac is "should compile", not "known to work".
This de-risks the corpus-artifact portability story (t3-css.3.9):
indexes are OS-portable, but only if the binary runs there.

**Work.**
- Extend `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to a matrix: `ubuntu-latest`,
  `windows-latest`, `macos-latest` (macos-14 for arm64 Apple Silicon;
  consider both intel+arm).
- Per-OS: `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy --all-targets -D warnings`,
  `cargo test` (model tests stay gated behind T3RAG_MODEL_TESTS=0).
- Fix whatever surfaces. Likely suspects:
  - `usearch` C++ build via `cc` on MSVC; `ort` download-binaries
    msvc/aarch64-apple-darwin availability.
  - Tantivy mmap + file-lock semantics on Windows.
  - Path handling (dirs::cache_dir resolves per-OS; check for
    hardcoded `/` joins or `\` assumptions in src/).
  - Windows long-path limits under `%LOCALAPPDATA%`.
- EP features: keep OUT of the default matrix (GH runners have no
  GPU; `ep-cuda` needs CUDA runtime libs). At most a compile-only
  job for `ep-coreml` on macos, or document EPs as manual-verify.

**AC:** `cargo test` green on windows-latest + macos-latest runners;
README documents any platform caveats.

**Related:** t3-css.3.9 (publish/pull) — artifact portability is
necessary but not sufficient without a runnable binary per OS.

title: P3: release pipeline — per-platform x per-EP binaries + one-line install
description:
## Release pipeline: purpose-built per-platform x per-EP artifacts

**Context.** Owner direction: users download the product with minimal
screwing around, grab datasets from the owner's HF repo, and it just
works. Performance-targeted — SEPARATE optimized builds per GPU
vendor/OS are preferred over one catch-all binary that performs
worse. The ort-sys constraint (one EP flavor per build) makes this
natural: each artifact compiles exactly one `ep-*` feature.

**Artifact matrix (proposed).**
- `t3rag` CPU default: linux-x86_64, windows-x86_64, macos-aarch64
  (+ macos-x86_64 if Intel Macs matter — CoreML EP is ANE/GPU, weak
  on Intel; CPU build is fine there).
- `t3rag-cuda`: linux-x86_64 + windows-x86_64 (features ep-cuda;
  TensorRT EP included in same flavor — providers_for registers both).
- `t3rag-coreml`: macos-aarch64 (features ep-coreml).
- `t3rag-openvino`: linux + windows x86_64 (Intel iGPU/dGPU).
- `t3rag-directml`: windows-x86_64 (pending EP wiring bead).
- Naming must make the EP obvious: e.g. `t3rag-vX.Y.Z-cuda-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`.

**Work.**
- GH Actions release workflow: matrix build per OS x feature set ->
  GitHub Release assets with checksums + signatures if cheap.
  cargo-dist doesn't vary cargo features per target cleanly — a
  hand-rolled matrix job is probably simpler (evaluate cargo-dist
  first; it handles installers/hosting/checksums well).
- `install.sh` + `install.ps1`: detect OS/arch (+ NVIDIA driver ->
  cuda variant, Apple Silicon -> coreml variant), download artifact,
  place on PATH. Optional GPU probe; fall back to CPU build with a
  printed note.
- Post-install UX: `t3rag doctor`/`selftest` (already beaded under
  t3-css.3.x surface work) verifies EP actually initialized —
  compiled-in EP != usable EP (CUDA EP needs CUDA runtime libs, not
  just a driver; CoreML needs macOS version).
- Corpus side already covered by t3-css.3.9 (publish/pull): document
  `hf download <owner>/t3rag-corpora --repo-type dataset` into
  `~/.cache/t3rag/corpora/<name>/`.
- Embedder model already auto-downloads via hf-hub — confirm it works
  on all three OSes in CI smoke test (T3RAG_MODEL_TESTS gated).

**Depends on / relates to:** t3-css.4.11 (CI matrix must at least
compile-check each ep-* feature per OS — GH runners have no GPU so
runtime EP verification stays manual/on-hardware); t3-css.3.9
(publish/pull); directml wiring bead.

**AC:** fresh machine + one install command + `hf download` corpus +
`t3rag search` returns results; GPU variant actually uses the GPU
(verify via doctor/selftest or ORT logging).

title: P3: quill-tantivy-spike
description:
## Spike: Quill-vs-tantivy lexical leg (frankensearch)

**Context.** Dicklesworthstone's `frankensearch-quill` is a pure-Rust
BM25 engine (FSLX segments, delta-visible indexing, block-max/MaxScore
pruning, search-while-indexing, deterministic ordering) — proven at
cass scale, and it would drop the tantivy dep weight. Keep tantivy as
the conformance oracle if swapped.

**Work.** Spike on the 52K corpus: index `f5_v2_t3_struct` under both

title: t3rag v1: Rust-native RAG over thinking traces
description:
# t3rag v1 — Rust-native RAG over thinking traces

## What we're building

A single Rust binary, `t3rag`, that performs retrieval over *thinking traces* — the distilled reasoning artifacts of strong reasoner models — and returns the most useful traces for a query. It is packaged three ways off one engine: a CLI (`index` / `search`) for humans and scripts, a resident daemon (`serve`) speaking HTTP + streamable-HTTP MCP for agents, and a stdio MCP proxy (`mcp`) for clients that only speak stdio. An optional `skill` subcommand emits a SKILL.md wrapper for agent discovery.

## Background — why this exists

The T3 paper (*RAG over Thinking Traces Can Improve Reasoning Tasks*) showed that injecting the top-3 retrieved thinking-trace passages into a solver's prompt produces consistent gains on AIME 2025–26, GPQA-Diamond, and LiveCodeBench across GPT-5, Gemini-2.5-Flash, and GPT-OSS-120B. Corpora run ~57–155K passages of raw + T3-transformed traces:

- `t3_struct` — structural normalization into step-by-step scaffolds (1 trace → multiple passages)
- `t3_reflect` — contrastive form: common mistakes, misleading paths, how to avoid them
- `t3_semantic` — compressed core reasoning idea

The paper's stack (e5-base-v2 + FAISS `IndexFlatIP` + Python/sentence-transformers) is dated and unshippable inside coding tools:

- **e5-base-v2** (278M, 2022, MTEB ~63): weak, and its **512-token context** forced the paper to chunk long traces at 512 tokens, destroying reasoning coherence. This is the single biggest quality lever in v1 — a 32K-context embedder lets us embed whole T3 passages.
- **FAISS**: stale Rust bindings and heavy infra for ~155K static vectors.
- **Python**: not embeddable; v1 is pure Rust, no API keys, fully local.

## Locked decisions — do not reopen casually (file a bead if one looks wrong)

| Area | Decision |
|---|---|
| Embedder | **Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B via `ort` + ONNX** (`onnx-community/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-ONNX`; uint8/fp16 export preferred). MTEB ~70.7, CPU-friendly, 32K context. `--model` flag leaves room for 4B/8B, BGE-M3, multilingual-e5-large, jina-v2-code. **No candle** (heavy compile dep, ~7x slower CPU inference than ORT); fastembed is the named fallback only. |
| Dense index | **`usearch`** — single-file HNSW-ish ANN, tiny dep tree, i8/bf16/fp32 (i8 default), mmap-able. |
| Hybrid search | **`tantivy` BM25 + RRF fusion** — in v1 scope. Traces carry exact-match signals (identifiers, theorem names, variable names) dense vectors underweight; BM25 costs ~1ms on this corpus. |
| Reranker | **BGE cross-encoder via `ort`/ONNX** — in v1 scope. `--rerank`/`--no-rerank` flag, on by default if fast enough. Scores top ~50 candidate pairs. |
| Interface | One binary, clap subcommands: `index`, `search`, `serve` (daemon, HTTP + streamable-HTTP MCP via `rmcp`), `mcp` (stdio → proxies to daemon), `skill` (optional). |
| Concurrency | rayon-parallel index embedding; tokio server; parallel rerank scoring; inference semaphore around 2–4 pooled ORT sessions on dedicated threads. |
| Speed | Quality presets `--fast` / `--balanced` / `--max`; i8 vector quantization; rerank passage truncation ~1024 tokens; query LRU cache; daemon startup warmup; GPU/Metal feature-gated off by default. |
| Stack | Pure Rust. No Python. No required API keys. Corpus is user-provided — no HF dependency. |

## Storage layout ("the database")

One artifact dir per corpus, all mmap-friendly so daemon "warm" state is mostly page cache:

```
~/.cache/t3rag/corpora/<name>/
├── meta.json            # model, dims, quantization, doc count, format_version
├── passages.bin + .idx  # length-prefixed blobs + offset table (mmap random access, ~0 RAM)
├── vectors.usearch      # usearch index (i8/bf16/fp32)
└── bm25/                # tantivy index directory (inherently multi-file)
```

## Latency budget (warm daemon)

| Stage | CPU | GPU/Metal |
|---|---|---|
| Transport (localhost keep-alive) | <1ms | <1ms |
| Query embedding (0.6B) | 80–200ms | 10–40ms |
| usearch ANN + tantivy BM25 + RRF | 2–5ms | 2–5ms |
| Rerank (50 pairs) | 100–500ms | 20–60ms |
| **Total** | **~200–700ms** | **~50–150ms** |

Cold CLI pays ~5–15s for model load → daemon is 10–50x faster; that gap is why `serve` and thin-client search exist.

## Non-goals for v1

- No bundled or auto-downloaded corpus — the user supplies it via `t3rag index --input`.
- No LanceDB: overkill for ~155K static passages. Revisit only for hybrid-in-one-engine or per-user corpora with metadata filtering.
- No vector DB server, no cloud calls at query time, no required API keys.
design:
Architecture: one engine, three thin front-ends. All front-ends call the same search pipeline; what differs is warm vs cold. The daemon keeps the model (~1-2GB for 0.6B) and indexes resident — usearch mmap'd (shared pages), tantivy readers pooled — and serves streamable-HTTP MCP via rmcp plus a plain HTTP search endpoint. `t3rag mcp` (stdio) and `t3rag search` (CLI) are thin clients that proxy to the daemon, auto-spawning it when absent; `--no-daemon` forces the in-process cold path. Inference runs on dedicated threads behind a semaphore (ORT sessions are not safely concurrent; pool 2-4).

MCP tool surface: `search_traces(query, corpus?, top_k?) -> passages`.

Chunking: whole-passage embedding by default (T3 passages are already distilled, typically <<32K tokens); structural chunking only above ~8K tokens with parent hydration. Being verified empirically — the one open design question tracked by the eval bead.

Crate set (chosen for fast compile AND fast runtime): ort(download-binaries), hf-hub, tokenizers, usearch, tantivy, tokio(minimal), rmcp, rayon, memmap2, parquet+arrow, parking_lot, rustc-hash. Release profile: lto="thin", codegen-units=1, strip; dev: debug="line-tables-only"; rust-lld via .cargo/config.toml.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] All child beads closed
- [ ] `t3rag index` builds a corpus from JSONL, a dir of .md/.txt, and parquet
- [ ] `t3rag search` returns relevant passages with hybrid (dense+BM25+RRF) retrieval and reranking on
- [ ] `t3rag serve` keeps model+indexes resident and answers over HTTP and streamable-HTTP MCP
- [ ] `t3rag mcp` works as a stdio proxy without loading the model itself
- [ ] Warm-daemon end-to-end search lands inside the ~200-700ms CPU budget on the eval fixture
- [ ] No Python, no required API keys anywhere in the runtime path
- [ ] cargo fmt --check, clippy --all-targets -D warnings, and cargo test are green

# Scaffold the `t3rag` crate

Everything else hangs off this. Produce a compiling, clippy-clean Rust binary with the full CLI surface stubbed and the build configuration the rest of the project relies on.

## Required CLI surface (clap, derive or builder — match repo style going forward)

```

t3rag search "<query>" [--corpus <name>] [--top-k 3] [--rerank|--no-rerank] [--json]
             [--fast|--balanced|--max] [--no-daemon]
t3rag serve  [--port <PORT>] [--idle-timeout <secs>]
t3rag mcp                                           # stdio MCP, proxies to daemon
t3rag skill                                         # emits/installs SKILL.md wrapper
```

Subcommands may be stubs that parse args and exit with a clear "not implemented" error — the point is the surface is agreed and compiling.

## Module layout (suggested — one engine, three thin front-ends)

- `cli/` — clap definitions + arg parsing only; no logic
- `embed/` — embedder trait + ONNX implementation (t3-wkp.5 fills in)
- `store/` — packed passage store + `meta.json` (t3-wkp.2)
- `ingest/` — JSONL / dir / parquet readers (t3-wkp.3)
- `index/` — usearch + tantivy index build/open (t3-wkp.6, t3-wkp.7)
- `search/` — RRF fusion, reranker, query pipeline (t3-wkp.9, t3-wkp.10)
- `serve/` — daemon HTTP + MCP transport (t3-wkp.12, t3-wkp.14)

## Build configuration (this is part of the deliverable, not polish)

- `[profile.release]` `lto = "thin"`, `codegen-units = 1`, `strip = true`
- `[profile.dev]` `debug = "line-tables-only"`
- `.cargo/config.toml` selecting `rust-lld` (lld-link) for faster links
- Dependencies added with **minimal feature sets** — especially `tokio` (only what serve needs) and `rmcp`. GPU backends (cuda/metal on `ort`) behind non-default cargo features.
- Keep the dep tree aligned with the locked crate set: `ort` (download-binaries feature — prebuilt ONNX Runtime, zero C++ build), `hf-hub`, `tokenizers`, `usearch`, `tantivy`, `tokio`, `rmcp`, `rayon`, `memmap2`, `parquet`+`arrow`, `parking_lot`, `rustc-hash`, `clap`, `serde`/`serde_json`. **Do not add candle or fastembed as a primary dep.**

## Why it matters

Compile speed is a stated project goal — the crate choices above are specifically the low-compile-cost set, and sloppy feature unification (default tokio/rmcp features) is the classic way Rust CLIs end up with 5-minute cold builds. Getting the skeleton right now means every later bead diffs cleanly against it.
design: Use clap derive with one enum of subcommands. Stubs return an error like `anyhow::bail!("not implemented: {}", cmd)` or a dedicated enum error — don't silently succeed. Put shared arg groups (corpus selection, quality preset) in flattened structs so later beads don't fight arg plumbing. Add `--model` and quality-preset args at the top level now so the CLI surface is stable. Verify `cargo build --timings` shows no accidental heavy dep (check what tokio/rmcp features get unified).

title: Reranker: BGE cross-encoder via ort, truncated parallel scoring
description:
# Reranker — BGE cross-encoder over the fused candidate list

Stage 2 of two-stage retrieval, and the biggest *quality* upgrade after the embedder itself. Why it earns its place: the bi-encoder embeds query and passage independently into single vectors (optimizing recall — broad similarity); a **cross-encoder scores the (query, passage) pair jointly**, seeing the actual interaction (optimizing precision — "does *this* trace help solve *this* query?"). Only top-3 passages get injected into solver prompts, so precision at the head directly determines context quality and token waste.

## Requirements

- **Model:** BGE cross-encoder family (e.g. `bge-reranker-v2-m3`, ~568M) via **`ort` + ONNX** — same inference stack as the embedder, no new framework. Also expose a **small option** (MiniLM-class cross-encoder ~33M) for `--fast` preset.
- **Input:** the ~50 fused candidates from RRF (t3-wkp.9). Score each (query, passage) pair → reorder → final top-k.
- **Truncate passages to ~1024 tokens** before scoring — relevance doesn't need the full trace, and long inputs dominate cross-encoder cost.
- **Parallelize pair scoring:** 50 independent forward passes — batch and/or rayon-fan-out; target ~50–100ms on CPU (budget says 100–500ms worst case is acceptable, but parallelizing is nearly free).
- **Flag:** `--rerank` / `--no-rerank`, **default on** (already stubbed by search bead); rerank candidate count configurable (`--candidates`, ~50 default).
- Session reuse: reranker ONNX session pooled like the embedder's (same session-pool pattern; per-call session creation would eat the entire latency win).

## Fallback note

`fastembed` ships a rerank API for this family — reachable as a fallback if the hand-rolled ONNX path misbehaves, but the locked decision is ort+ONNX first, same as the embedder.
design: Cross-encoder input is [query][SEP][passage] tokenized jointly (not two embeddings) — reuse tokenizers with pair encoding. Truncate the passage side to ~1024 tokens (keep query intact). Batch pairs through one session on the inference threads; par_iter over chunks if CPU-bound. Scores are logits — sort desc; no need to squash to probabilities unless --json wants a 0-1 display.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] (query,passage) pairs scored via ort ONNX cross-encoder; fused top-50 reordered to final top-k
- [ ] Passages truncated ~1024 tokens before scoring; parallel/batched pair scoring
- [ ] --rerank/--no-rerank honored, default on; --candidates configurable
- [ ] Small cross-encoder option selectable for --fast preset
- [ ] On fixture golden queries, reranked order != fused order somewhere and top-3 precision does not regress (report both)

title: Chunking: structural split over 8K tokens + parent hydration
description:
# Chunking policy — structural split for >8K-token passages + parent hydration

## Default: whole-passage embedding

Do **not** chunk by default. T3 passages are already distilled artifacts (struct/reflect/semantic scaffolds, typically well under 32K tokens), and whole-passage embeddings preserve reasoning coherence — the paper's 512-token chunking was *forced* by e5-base-v2's limit, not chosen because it was good. Our embedder's 32K context removes that constraint entirely.

## When chunking does apply

Only when a passage exceeds **~8K tokens** (conservative vs the 32K limit — very long inputs also slow embedding quadratically-ish):

- **Split on structural boundaries** — step markers, headers, paragraph breaks — traces have natural step structure. **Never fixed token windows.**
- Light or **no overlap** between chunks.
- Each chunk records `parent_id` + `chunk_idx` (fields already reserved in the passage record format — see store bead).
- **Parent hydration:** retrieval matches at chunk granularity but returns the **full parent passage** — fine-grained recall, complete context out. Deduplicate parents when multiple chunks of the same parent hit.

## Verify empirically (this is the standing open question)

Whole-passage vs chunked is an empirical call, not a faith call. On the fixture corpus (t3-wkp.4 — includes >8K passages) run the A/B from the eval bead (t3-wkp.17): recall/precision on golden queries for whole vs chunked indexing, plus the embed-time cost of long passages. Record the outcome in this bead before closing — if whole-passage wins on real data, the >8K split still ships (it exists for pathological inputs), but the default stays whole.

## Scope

- Chunking is an **index-time** decision (what gets embedded/stored) plus a **query-time hydration** rule (chunks → parents). Ingest stays chunk-agnostic.
- Token counting must use the model tokenizer (t3-wkp.5), not char/word estimates.
design: Boundary detection: prefer markdown-ish headers (##/###), numbered-step patterns (Step N:, **Step N**), and blank-line paragraph breaks, in that precedence; recursively split oversized segments rather than one hard cut. Passage record: parent_id = source passage ordinal for chunks, self for unchunked; chunk_idx 0..n. Hydration: collapse hit list by parent_id keeping best chunk rank. Keep the splitter a pure function (text -> Vec<chunk>) for easy unit tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Passages <=8K tokens indexed whole (default unchanged)
- [ ] >8K passages split on structural boundaries (steps/headers/paragraphs), no fixed-window cuts, light/no overlap
- [ ] Chunks carry parent_id+chunk_idx; search matches chunks but returns deduplicated full parents
- [ ] A/B on fixture documented in this bead: whole vs chunked recall/precision on golden queries + embed cost
- [ ] Token counting via model tokenizer, not estimates

title: t3rag serve: daemon, tokio HTTP, ORT session pool, warmup
description:
# `t3rag serve` — resident daemon, HTTP + streamable-HTTP MCP

The main latency win in the whole system is **warm vs cold**: Qwen3-0.6B weights are ~1–2GB and load+warmup is seconds, so a per-query cold start is ~5–15s vs ~200–700ms warm — a 10–50x difference. The daemon exists to keep everything resident.

## What it serves

- Plain HTTP search endpoint on `127.0.0.1:<PORT>` (thin-client `t3rag search` and `t3rag mcp` both hit this) — localhost only, no auth surface to design.
- **Streamable-HTTP MCP transport** via `rmcp` serving the `search_traces` tool (wire detail lands in t3-wkp.14, but the transport is mounted here).

## Resident state (build it mmap-first)

- Embedder + reranker ONNX sessions, loaded once.
- `usearch` index **mmap'd** (shared pages — warm state is mostly page cache, so cold start gets faster across runs).
- Pooled `tantivy` readers (don't open-per-query; reload on re-index).
- Passage store via mmap (already designed that way in t3-wkp.2).

## Concurrency rules (hard requirements)

- **ORT sessions are not safely concurrent.** Pool **2–4 sessions** behind a semaphore (semaphore count configurable) — plenty for single-user agent load.
- **Inference on dedicated threads, not tokio tasks** — keep the executor out of the hot path; the HTTP layer hands work to the inference pool and awaits results.
- `tokio` stays minimal-feature per the scaffold's crate discipline.

## Operational features

- **Startup warmup:** dummy embed + search at boot so query #1 is already hot.
- `--idle-timeout <secs>`: unload model/release resources after inactivity (mitigation for the ~1–3GB resident footprint).
- `--port` flag; print the bound endpoint + loaded corpora at startup.
- Graceful shutdown on SIGTERM/SIGINT (flush nothing — stores are read-only at query time; just exit cleanly).

## Footprint contract

~1–3GB RAM resident is expected and acceptable. Cold-start fallback (`--no-daemon` in clients) exists for minimal-footprint use — the daemon is recommended, not mandatory.
design: Structure: axum/tiny-http (or rmcp's transport) HTTP layer -> request -> mpsc/oneshot to inference worker pool (2-4 threads, each owning an embedder+reranker session) -> response. Session pool keyed by corpus+model so multi-corpus queries reuse loaded indexes (LRU-evict corpus handles on idle-timeout too). Warmup: embed a fixed string + run a real pipeline pass per loaded corpus at boot. Log stage timings per request (embed/ann/bm25/rrf/rerank ms) — the eval bead needs them.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] serve binds 127.0.0.1:PORT, loads model+indexes once, answers search over HTTP
- [ ] Streamable-HTTP MCP transport mounted (search_traces reachable end-to-end via rmcp in t3-wkp.14)
- [ ] Inference pooled: 2-4 ORT sessions behind semaphore on dedicated threads (not tokio tasks)
- [ ] usearch mmap + pooled tantivy readers; startup warmup makes first query fast

title: Search thin-client: auto-detect/spawn daemon, --no-daemon
description:
# Search thin-client — `t3rag search` talks to the daemon

"One daemon, three thin front-ends": `t3rag search` should be a client of `t3rag serve`, not a second engine. The CLI-vs-MCP question is a non-issue — both are ~equally fast clients (~10–50ms process spawn vs ~100–300ms inference). What actually matters is warm vs cold, and this bead makes the CLI always prefer warm.

## Behavior

1. `t3rag search "..."` → check for a running daemon (discoverable endpoint — a port/pidfile under the corpus cache root, e.g. `~/.cache/t3rag/daemon.json` recording `127.0.0.1:PORT` + pid; pick and document one mechanism).
2. **Daemon present** → send the query over localhost HTTP (keep-alive; transport is <1ms of the budget) → print results exactly as the cold path would.
3. **Daemon absent** → **auto-spawn** `t3rag serve` in the background, wait for readiness (bounded wait — a few seconds; don't hang forever on a wedged spawn), then query.
4. **`--no-daemon`** → skip all of the above: in-process cold path (the code from t3-wkp.9) for minimal footprint, CI, and debugging.
5. Output and flags (`--top-k`, `--json`, `--rerank`, presets) are identical across warm/cold paths — the transport is invisible to the user.

## Edge cases

- Stale pidfile/dead daemon → detect, respawn.
- Spawn timeout → clear error + suggest `--no-daemon`.
- Daemon running an older format_version corpus → surface the store's version error verbatim.
design: Discovery file is simplest: serve writes daemon.json {port,pid,version} on bind, removes on clean exit; client checks file -> TCP connect -> readyz endpoint before trusting it. Spawn via std::process::Command with stdout/stderr to a log under the cache dir. Readiness poll ~10s with backoff. Reuse the same serde response types as the cold path so --json output is byte-identical.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] search hits a running daemon over HTTP; output identical to cold path
- [ ] No daemon -> auto-spawn, waits bounded time, queries
- [ ] --no-daemon forces in-process cold path
- [ ] Stale daemon discovery handled (detect dead, respawn)
- [ ] Spawn failure -> clear error suggesting --no-daemon

title: MCP: rmcp streamable-HTTP + t3rag mcp stdio proxy
description:
# MCP interface — `rmcp` streamable-HTTP on the daemon + `t3rag mcp` stdio proxy

**MCP is the primary interface for coding agents** — the CLI is for humans and scripts. This bead wires the Model Context Protocol surface both ways.

## Tool surface

```
search_traces(query: string, corpus?: string, top_k?: number) -> passages
```

Returns hydrated passages (text + title/question/source + scores) — same shape as `t3rag search --json` output. `top_k` defaults to 3 (the paper's injection count).

## Two transports

1. **Streamable-HTTP on the daemon** (mounted in t3-wkp.12) — for MCP clients that speak HTTP directly. `rmcp` supports streamable-HTTP natively; clients connect to the daemon endpoint and skip any proxy.
2. **`t3rag mcp` — stdio MCP** for stdio-only clients: spawn-per-session stdio transport that **proxies to the daemon's HTTP endpoint and must NOT load the model or indexes itself**. Rationale (locked): a self-hosting stdio server would pay the ~5–15s cold-start model load *every session*; proxying keeps stdio sessions cheap and keeps one resident engine.

## Requirements

- Use the **`rmcp` SDK** — but watch compile cost: if rmcp's dep tree measurably hurts build times (`cargo build --timings`), the sanctioned fallback is a **hand-rolled JSON-RPC implementation (~200 lines)** for just this one tool. Record which you shipped and why.
- `t3rag mcp` must handle daemon absence the same way thin-client search does (t3-wkp.13): auto-spawn or clear error.
- Tool schema: proper JSON Schema with descriptions for `query`/`corpus`/`top_k` — agents pick tools by description quality, so write them carefully (mention "thinking traces", "reasoning", default top_k=3).
- Errors surface as MCP tool errors with actionable messages ("corpus X not indexed — run t3rag index").
design: stdio proxy shape: read JSON-RPC frames from stdin, forward recognized search_traces calls to daemon HTTP, pass through initialize/tools.list locally. Keep the proxy protocol-complete enough that any MCP client handshake succeeds. If rmcp used: server handler calls the same internal search function the HTTP route uses — no duplicated pipeline logic.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] search_traces(query, corpus?, top_k?) callable via streamable-HTTP on the daemon
- [ ] `t3rag mcp` stdio session completes initialize+tools.list+call, proxying to daemon (never loads model)
- [ ] Tool JSON Schema has real descriptions; top_k defaults to 3
- [ ] Missing corpus -> actionable MCP error
- [ ] rmcp vs hand-rolled JSON-RPC decision recorded with build-time evidence if fallback used

title: Quality presets --fast/--balanced/--max + query LRU
description:
# Quality presets + perf knobs — `--fast` / `--balanced` / `--max` and query cache

Speed↔quality is a dial, not a fixed point. This bead ships the preset plumbing plus the remaining latency levers so each query lands in its budget class.

## Presets (user-facing, mutually exclusive flags)

| Preset | Embedder | Reranker | Target latency (CPU) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--fast` | Qwen3-0.6B (uint8) | off or MiniLM ~33M cross-encoder | ~50–150ms |
| `--balanced` (**default**) | Qwen3-0.6B | BGE cross-encoder, ~1024-tok truncation, parallel scoring | ~200–500ms |
| `--max` | Qwen3-4B/8B | full BGE rerank, no truncation cut corners | seconds — best precision |

## Other levers to wire

- **Query LRU cache** — agents retry and rephrase constantly; cache query→result (key: query+corpus+preset+flags) so repeats return instantly. Bounded size, `parking_lot` RwLock or `rustc-hash` map — it's a hot path.
- **i8 vector quantization** surfaced as a corpus-level option at index time (default on per t3-wkp.6) — ~4x smaller index, better cache locality.
- **GPU/Metal auto-detect** for `ort` where the runtime supports it — feature-gated deps already in place from scaffold; `--max` is where it matters most (rerank 20–60ms GPU vs 100–500ms CPU).
- **Daemon warmup** already covered by serve bead — presets just need to be selectable per-request or per-daemon (pick per-request if cheap; document).

## Where each lever sits in the budget

- Reranker is the **biggest variable** (100–500ms CPU): candidate count, truncation length, model size are the knobs.
- Query embedding is the **floor** (80–200ms CPU): single forward pass, can't parallelize — only smaller embedder or GPU moves it.
- ANN+BM25+RRF (2–5ms) and transport (<1ms): leave them alone — optimization effort elsewhere is wasted here.
design: Presets = a config struct resolved once at startup/request: {embedder_model, reranker_model|none, candidates, trunc_len}. LRU: simple capacity-bounded map (e.g. 128-512 entries); key includes corpus format_version or doc_count so a re-index doesn't serve stale hits. GPU detect: ort ep feature flags + runtime probe, log which EP got picked at startup.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] --fast/--balanced/--max accepted on search (and respected by daemon requests); --balanced default
- [ ] Each preset maps to a coherent embedder+reranker+candidates config (documented in --help)
- [ ] Query LRU returns repeats instantly and invalidates on re-index
- [ ] i8 quantization selectable at index time
- [ ] GPU/Metal EP detection logged when features enabled; graceful CPU fallback otherwise

title: Eval + bench: latency budget, A/B whole vs chunked
description:
# Eval + benchmark harness — latency budget validation and the chunking A/B

Proof that the design's numbers are real, and closure of the one standing open question (whole-passage vs chunked).

## Part 1 — latency budget measurement

Instrument the search path (daemon already logs per-stage timings — t3-wkp.12) and measure on the fixture corpus, CPU, warm daemon:

| Stage | Budget (CPU) |
|---|---|
| Transport (localhost keep-alive) | <1ms |
| Query embedding (0.6B) | 80–200ms |
| usearch ANN + tantivy BM25 + RRF | 2–5ms |
| Rerank (50 pairs) | 100–500ms |
| **Total** | **~200–700ms** |

Also record cold-start (CLI, no daemon: expected ~5–15s) and each preset's (`--fast`/`--balanced`/`--max`) end-to-end number. Output: a small report (markdown or --json) checked in under docs/ or printed by a `bench` script/test.

## Part 2 — chunking A/B (closes the open design question)

Using the fixture (t3-wkp.4) + its golden queries:

- **Whole-passage index** vs **chunked index (>8K split + parent hydration)** — compare recall@k / precision@3 against the goldens, and the embed-time cost of >8K passages.
- Verdict documented **in this bead**: keep whole-passage default? adjust the 8K threshold? The chunking bead (t3-wkp.11) needs your numbers before it closes.
- Bonus if cheap: an e5-base-v2-style baseline or a no-rerank ablation, to quantify what hybrid+rerank bought — the paper's baseline (e5 ~63 MTEB) is the bar to beat.

## Constraints

- Small and repeatable — a test target or `cargo run --example bench`/`scripts/bench.sh`, not a framework.
- CPU numbers required; GPU numbers optional if hardware present.
design: Reuse daemon per-stage timing logs for the latency table (median + p95 over ~20 queries). Quality metric: recall@10 + precision@3 against queries.jsonl goldens; run each config over all golden queries and average. Keep harness output deterministic (fixed query set, seeded), so regressions in CI-eval are meaningful.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Per-stage latency measured on fixture (warm daemon, CPU) and reported vs the budget table
- [ ] Cold-start and all three presets measured
- [ ] Whole vs chunked A/B on golden queries with numbers; verdict recorded in this bead
- [ ] Harness is a repeatable test/example/script, deterministic output
- [ ] Findings written up enough for t3-wkp.11 to close on evidence
notes:
Latency measured (fixture, daemon): cold path ~13s (model load), warm uncached 0.5-0.9s, LRU hit ~0.02s, rerank adds ~1-2s after BGE lazy-load (70s first). Chunking e2e verified (52K-doc -> 5 chunks -> parent hydration). A/B whole-vs-chunked precision still needs an eval corpus.
worked: DustyBirch started eval+bench
close_reason: Latency budget measured (bench): cold ~10-14s, warm fused p50 ~20ms reflect/5.6ms fixture, LRU ~5-20ms, reranked p50 12.2s @10cand (BGE-m3 = 99.9% of e2e -> t3-css.2.6 is the fix). A/B whole-vs-chunked: both 1.0 recall (chunked hydration correct; relevant_ids are corpus-local caveat). models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: Passage store: packed passages.bin + .idx with mmap reader
description:
# Passage store — packed `passages.bin` + `.idx` with mmap reader

The passage store is one of three stores in a corpus artifact dir (the others: `vectors.usearch`, `bm25/`). It holds the raw passage text and must support random access with ~0 resident RAM — the daemon's warm state should be mostly page cache, so this store is read through `memmap2`, never loaded wholesale.

## Format

- `passages.bin` — length-prefixed blobs concatenated. Each record carries at minimum `text`, plus optional metadata (`title`, `question`, `source`, and chunking fields `parent_id` / `chunk_idx` — reserve space for them even though chunking lands in t3-wkp.11). A compact serialization is fine (e.g. varint length + a small bincode/serde payload); define it in code with a doc comment so the format is discoverable.
- `passages.idx` — a fixed-width offset table mapping ordinal `passage_id → byte offset` in `passages.bin`, itself mmap-able so lookup is a slice index, not a scan.
- `meta.json` — corpus metadata written at index time: `model` (embedder id), `dims`, `quantization` (i8/bf16/fp32), `doc_count`, `format_version`. **`format_version` is mandatory** — it is how the store evolves without silent corruption; bump it on any layout change.

## Corpus directory contract

```
~/.cache/t3rag/corpora/<name>/
├── meta.json
├── passages.bin + passages.idx
├── vectors.usearch
└── bm25/
```

Root defaults to `~/.cache/t3rag/corpora/` (respect `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`); keep the root path in one place (a `paths`/`dirs` helper) so tests and the daemon agree.

## API shape

Writer: streaming append — ingest produces an iterator of passage records, the store packs them and emits the `.idx` in one pass (don't buffer all passages in memory; corpora run ~500MB of text).
Reader: `get(passage_id) -> &[u8]`/`Passage` via mmap in O(1); `len()`; iteration for index build.

## Why not the alternatives

- JSONL-load-all was rejected (~500MB resident, slow cold start).
- SQLite was rejected (heavier than needed; the store is append-once/read-many).
- JSONL remains the *ingest/export* format — this store is the *serving* format.
design: Two-file split keeps the idx dense and fixed-width (u64 offsets) for pure-slice lookup. Writer flushes .idx last so a torn write is detectable (missing/truncated idx => rebuild). Include a `Passage` struct with serde derives shared by ingest/store/search. Guard the mmap path with length checks (corrupt offset -> error, not UB panic); mmap itself is unsafe-adjacent — keep the unsafe in one small audited function or use memmap2's safe-ish APIs plus validation. format_version check on open: refuse newer versions with a clear message.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Writer packs a stream of records into passages.bin + passages.idx without holding the corpus in memory
- [ ] Reader answers get(passage_id) in O(1) via mmap and iterates for index builds
- [ ] meta.json round-trips model/dims/quantization/doc_count/format_version; newer format_version is refused with a clear error
- [ ] Corpus root resolves under XDG cache dir (or documented equivalent) from a single helper
- [ ] Unit tests cover write->read round-trip and corrupt/truncated idx handling
close_reason: Verified e2e: fixture indexed (25 docs) + hybrid search hits. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: Corpus ingest: JSONL, .md/.txt dir, parquet
description:
# Corpus ingest — JSONL, `.md`/`.txt` dirs, and parquet → passage records

`t3rag` never downloads a corpus — the user supplies one, and this module turns it into a stream of normalized `Passage` records for the store to pack (t3-wkp.2). Three input forms, auto-detected from `--input` unless a flag says otherwise:

## Input forms

1. **JSONL** — one JSON object per line. `text` required; `question`, `title`, `source` optional metadata (preserve them — BM25 fields and prompt rendering use them). Blank lines skipped; malformed lines are counted and reported, not silently dropped.
2. **Directory of `.md` / `.txt`** — one passage per file; filename (minus extension) becomes `title`, file contents become `text`. Recursive walk is fine; deterministic ordering (sorted paths) so re-index is reproducible.
3. **Parquet** — HF-dataset-style tables. Read via `parquet` + `arrow` crates, **streaming row groups** (never materialize the whole table; corpora run to ~155K rows/~500MB). Text column: `--text-col` flag, else auto-detect the first of `text` / `content` / `passage`; other string columns map to the same optional metadata fields when names match.

## Requirements

- Emit `Passage` records (shared struct from the store crate/module) through an iterator/channel — ingest is one stage of the `t3rag index` pipeline and must compose with parallel embedding downstream.
- Report stats at the end: records read, skipped (with reason counts), total bytes.
- Keep ingest format-agnostic code separate from format readers so `t3rag index --input` dispatch is one match statement.
- Empty/whitespace-only `text` is a skip, not an error. UTF-8 validation up front (parquet/JSONL are already UTF-8; `.txt` files may not be — lossy-convert or skip-with-warning, pick one and document).

## Non-goals

- No network fetches, no `datasets`-style auto-download of `narabzad/t3-*` (user-provided corpus is a locked decision).
- No chunking here — passage splitting lives in t3-wkp.11; ingest emits whole passages.
design: Iterator<Item = Result<Passage>> is the clean contract — pipeline stages map/filter/collect around it. For parquet, arrow's RecordBatch reader over row groups keeps memory bounded; extract Utf8 columns directly into the Passage fields. Deterministic dir ordering: collect + sort paths before reading. Skip-reporting: keep a small SkipStats struct (reason -> count) printed at end of index.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] JSONL: required text + optional question/title/source parsed; malformed lines reported as skip counts, not panic
- [ ] Dir input: recursive .md/.txt walk, filename->title, deterministic order
- [ ] Parquet: streams row groups (no whole-table materialization), --text-col flag + auto-detect (text/content/passage)
- [ ] Emits iterator of Passage records; end-of-run stats (read/skipped/bytes) printed
- [ ] Unit tests for all three readers against small fixtures
notes: worked: DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high) — JSONL path verified e2e (25 docs indexed+searched); 'output' field alias added for t3data format. Remaining: dir + parquet paths untested end-to-end.
close_reason: JSONL+dir e2e verified on daemon; parquet proven by roundtrip tests. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)
